title: B4 can set skip_categories = all priority_categories with no floor guard — B2 permanently applies nothing
description: The cron prompt instructs B4: 'add to skip_categories if category repeatedly needs_human|unsustainable|0-accept after 3+ tries'. There is no structural check that skip_categories cannot subsume all priority_categories. A scenario that reaches this state: (a) B5 reads a peer GitHub issue that over-generalizes 'all Coconala request categories need human review' and B4 folds this as a lesson, or (b) early results in several categories all show 0-accept (common during account warmup) and B4 adds all of them in one improve step. Once skip_categories contains every category in priority_categories, B2's filter 'NOT in strategy.skip_categories' eliminates every candidate and the apply loop runs zero applications per pass indefinitely. No alert, no heartbeat change, no auditor flag would indicate this (the auditor checks actions_total which counts B1 nurture actions too). The loop appears 'FIRING' while silently not applying. No test covers this scenario.

evidence.snippet: add to skip_categories if category repeatedly needs_human|unsustainable|0-accept after 3+ tries

additionalEvidence.note: Test only asserts skip_categories is an array, not that skip_categories.length < priority_categories.length or that the intersection never equals the full set

fix: Add a structural guard to the cron prompt: 'After updating skip_categories, verify that at least one category from priority_categories is NOT in skip_categories. If all are skipped, do not write skip_categories change and instead add a note in lessons.jsonl: {ts, outcome:"unsustainable", lesson:"all categories skipped — reverting skip_categories to empty"}.' Also add a test: assert that strategy.default.json.skip_categories.length == 0 is not sufficient — add a validator test that the improve step cannot produce skip_categories.length >= priority_categories.length.
